limitations: The requested ApoMarioHighscore class and recordRunEnd method do not yet exist in the inspected repository, so their exact enforcement anchors cannot be resolved.
The default local store path, highscore menu button/node, and whether AI, replay, simulation, or editor runs should be eligible are not established by the inspected code.
No implementation or tests were added because the workspace is read-only.

Player performance displayed in the highscore panel
Finished-run values into highscore storage
nodes.sink: Prospective ApoMarioHighscore.recordRunEnd(ApoMarioLevel) and storeRun(int,int,String), followed by the Path-backed persistence operation.
nodes.source: ApoMarioLevel player state and completion/death flow: player points and team name, level countdown, and setAnalysis transition.
nodes.untrusted_input: Score, player name, and elapsed time can be altered by local tampering or cheating before the record operation.

nodes.label: User-controlled local highscore file into parser and display

nodes.untrusted_input: The local file supplied as the highscore store can contain malformed, truncated, oversized, reordered, or manually edited records.

nodes.label: Highscore panel navigation from the game menu
nodes.sink: Prospective dedicated highscore panel/view and ApoMarioPanel model/button state.

nodes.untrusted_input: Mouse and keyboard menu events are user-controlled and may select panel transitions or exercise unexpected navigation order.

nodes.label: ApoMario stores player points and exposes them through ApoMarioPlayer#getPoints(); player names are derived from ApoMarioPlayer#getTeamName(), while ApoMarioLevel#getTime() exposes the remaining level countdown and getPassedTime() derives elapsed time from the random level timer.
nodes.task_relevance: These are the existing sources that recordRunEnd must read and convert to score, name, and survival time.
nodes.verification: Unit-test a completed run and a losing run with known points, name, and timer values; assert the stored record contains those values and formats elapsed time as mm:ss.

nodes.label: ApoMario marks a run finished through ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean): the method sets the win state, updates points on a win, and transitions the ApoMarioPanel to analysis; player death and finish paths invoke setAnalysis from player/level logic.
nodes.task_relevance: recordRunEnd must be invoked once at this completion boundary after the final score adjustment and for both clearing and losing paths.
nodes.verification: Exercise finish and death scenarios and assert exactly one highscore record is added per run, after the final points calculation.

nodes.label: ApoIcarus separates parallel name, time, and points lists in ApoHighscore and its highscore state inserts records in descending points order before rendering names, points, and formatted time.
nodes.task_relevance: The donor structure and ordering behavior are reusable for ApoMarioHighscore, but the target API must replace the donor's online transport with a local Path store.
nodes.verification: Compare ApoMarioHighscore getter order after inserting records with ascending, descending, and tied scores against the required descending-score ordering.

nodes.failure_behavior: Observed code catches IOException but does not catch NumberFormatException from Integer.valueOf; malformed numeric input can escape as a runtime failure.
nodes.label: The donor ApoHighscore load operation parses every three input lines directly into Integer values and stores names without validating record count, integer range, or name content; malformed online response data can therefore raise parsing errors or create inconsistent parallel lists.
nodes.task_relevance: A local-file adaptation that copies this parser without validation would expose the new highscore store to malformed user-edited files.
nodes.verification: Feed malformed numeric lines, incomplete triplets, invalid UTF-8 if applicable, and oversized names to the parser and assert deterministic rejection/reporting without partial records.

nodes.failure_behavior: Proposed implementation must reject invalid records and report the rejection; it must not clamp or substitute values inside the parser.
nodes.label: A Path-backed highscore implementation could allow a user-edited file to inject arbitrary names, negative or overflowing values, mismatched record arrays, or enough records to consume memory before the panel renders them.
nodes.task_relevance: This boundary covers parsing, validation, allocation, sorting, getter exposure, and rendering of the new persisted board.
nodes.verification: Use property-based and boundary tests for record count, string length, integer range, malformed delimiters, and inconsistent records; verify rejection is reported and no unbounded allocation or partial board is exposed.

nodes.failure_behavior: At the integration point, normalize a missing or invalid name to the stated local default and normalize invalid score/time to stated safe values before calling storeRun; do not suppress the record effect.
nodes.label: Because score and name are mutable in-process game values and local users can load AI/replay content, recording those values without an explicit integration policy could let cheated or spoofed values become authoritative highscore entries.
nodes.task_relevance: The requirement says to record the running game's real score and player name; the integration must select the intended human/current-run player and exclude replay, simulation, editor, or invalid identities as defined by the implementation.
nodes.verification: Run with human, AI, replay, simulation, and editor modes; verify the selected record source, normalized defaults, and one-record-per-run behavior match the documented policy.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report the invalid file; retain a safe empty/in-memory state only as the caller's explicit recovery behavior, never as parser-level clamping or substitution.
nodes.label: The first operation receiving persisted highscore bytes must validate the file format, record cardinality, integer ranges, name encoding/length, and aligned name-score-time records; invalid input must be rejected and reported without clamping, substitution, partial insertion, or unbounded allocation.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects the integrity and availability of the Path-backed board while covering parsing and allocation before getters or rendering.
nodes.verification: Parser tests cover valid files, malformed fields, incomplete records, negative/overflow values, excessive lengths/counts, and I/O failures; assert rejection is observable and no partial record is returned.

nodes.failure_behavior: The integration caller normalizes missing or invalid values before storeRun so the record effect still occurs; storeRun itself rejects invalid arguments and reports the rejection.
nodes.label: At the run-end integration, record the final actual player score after the level's win/loss calculation, the selected player's real name with an explicit fallback for missing/invalid names, and elapsed survival time normalized to a nonnegative integer and displayed as mm:ss; invoke this for both clearing and losing a level exactly once.
nodes.task_relevance: Directly implements the requested run-end data flow and prevents spoofed or stale values from becoming the recorded entry.
nodes.verification: Test win and loss transitions with known final points and countdown values; assert one record, correct player name/fallback, nonnegative elapsed seconds, and mm:ss rendering.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject invalid storage writes and report I/O failure; retain the successful in-memory entry and do not claim persistence until the write completes.
nodes.label: storeRun and the persisted representation must preserve name-score-time association, sort entries by score descending, and persist successful entries across application runs; the panel must display the same aligned ordering through the required getters.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects highscore integrity and availability from reordering, truncation, or lost records.
nodes.verification: Store multiple entries, restart ApoMarioHighscore with the same temporary Path, call persistAcrossRuns, reload, and compare all three getter lists and rendered order.

nodes.failure_behavior: Parser rejects and reports invalid data; the caller reports the failure and uses an empty display model, without silently accepting, clamping, or allocating from attacker-controlled unbounded sizes.
nodes.label: At the ApoMarioHighscore file-load/parser operation, use bounded buffered reads and an explicit versioned record format; validate every field before constructing a record, keep the three collections aligned, and report parse/I/O rejection. At panel initialization, recover with an empty board after reporting the failure so menu operation continues.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces safe file ingestion while preserving the highscore panel's primary display effect.
nodes.verification: Integration-test malformed store files and unreadable paths, then assert an error is reported, the panel remains usable, and getters expose no partial or oversized data.

nodes.failure_behavior: Missing or invalid integration values are normalized before storeRun; a storeRun rejection is logged/reported and does not undo the run or suppress the attempt.
nodes.label: At ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean), guard the once-only run-end hook around the existing bAnalysis transition, read points/name/time after final scoring, select the active human run rather than replay/simulation/editor data, normalize missing names to a documented default and invalid score/time to documented safe defaults, then call storeRun and report any rejected entry.
nodes.task_relevance: Preserves the primary record effect while preventing stale, duplicate, or invalid in-game values from entering storage.
nodes.verification: Instrument the hook across repeated setAnalysis calls and all play modes; assert final-value ordering, normalization, exclusion policy, and exactly-once recording.

nodes.failure_behavior: Invalid records are rejected and reported; persistence errors are reported while the in-memory board remains available and displayed.
nodes.label: At storeRun, insert one immutable/validated record and sort or maintain all three lists together by descending score; at persistAcrossRuns, write atomically to the supplied file, report failures, and retain the in-memory successful entry. At panel initialization and highscore-view entry, load the file and render only validated aligned records.
nodes.task_relevance: Reuses the donor's parallel-list and descending-order behavior while adding local durability and preserving the display effect on write failure.
nodes.verification: Use temporary files and injected read/write failures; verify list alignment, descending order, atomic recovery behavior, error reporting, and continued panel rendering.

nodes.label: Run an end-to-end desktop test: create a temporary Path store, record both a completed and losing run, persist, construct a new ApoMarioHighscore from the same Path, and assert names, scores, survival times, descending order, and mm:ss display.
nodes.task_relevance: Verifies the full introduced flow from level state through storage, reload, sorting, and menu display.

nodes.label: The inspected ApoMario sources do not establish which existing button/node should open a dedicated highscore panel, nor which Path should be the default persistent store; the current menu handlers visibly cover start, options, credits, simulation, replay, editor, and quit but no highscore contract was resolved.
nodes.task_relevance: The implementing model must resolve the menu/button mapping and store location before integration tests can exercise the feature.
nodes.verification: Inspect ApoMarioButtons and button constants at implementation time, then add an integration test that selects the highscore node and verifies the dedicated view uses the configured Path.

summary: ApoMario already maintains player points, names, and a countdown-based elapsed-time source at level completion or death. ApoIcarus provides reusable highscore record structures and descending-score display logic, but its persistence is network-oriented; ApoMario needs a local Path-backed store and a menu panel integrated with the existing analysis/menu transitions.
